summary: Feed s182_triple is degraded: 16.3% duplicate packets, 100% VLAN tags stripped (VLANs 10,20 missing), and 24.36 Gbps bursts overloading 10 Gbps APM port (244% capacity).

findings.root_cause: Duplicate packets from overlapping SPAN/TAP feeds aggregated without deduplication on packet broker - same packet seen on multiple ingress ports forwarded to single APM tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM wastes CPU/storage on duplicates, inflates transaction counts and latency metrics, and skews application performance baselines.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker deduplication to drop identical packets within dedup window before delivery to APM, eliminating 16.3% waste without losing unique transactions.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags (VLAN stripping / SPAN not preserving tags) - all packets delivered untagged so required VLANs 10 and 20 are invisible.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot segment traffic by VLAN/tenant or tier (VLANs 10,20 required), losing application context and breaking per-VLAN dashboards and alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Configure broker ingress to preserve 802.1Q and forward VLANs 10,20 to APM; APM needs VLAN context for correct application mapping.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts to 24.36 Gbps exceed single 10 Gbps APM port capacity by 244% - aggregate throughput not shaped for tool port speed.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM NIC drops packets during bursts, causing incomplete flows, missed transactions, and inaccurate latency/error rates despite no broker drops yet.

recommended_fix.why: Load-balance feed across 2-3 APM ports/instances with flow-aware hashing to keep per-port rate <80% of 10G and preserve both directions per flow for APM.
